reasons: The redline reverses the ownership direction in § 14.2 exactly as the rule requires: Customer owns each Deliverable, with a present, irrevocable assignment from Vendor, and the offending revocable, term-limited licence-back-to-Customer sentence is removed as unnecessary once ownership vests in us.

The carve-out 'subject only to Vendor's retained rights in Vendor Technology under Section 14.3' preserves Vendor's pre-existing IP, consistent with the preferred position and avoiding an over-reach that would invite pushback.

The Deliverable definition (§ 1.4 — work product 'created specifically for Customer', excluding Vendor Technology and unaided know-how) confirms this is paid-for bespoke work product, so the finding is directionally correct and not a mislabelled platform-ownership clause.

Customer Data and Customer IP ownership is already handled in §§ 14.1/15.1 and joint ownership is disclaimed in § 14.4, so no additional sentences were needed; scoping the edit to the single defective paragraph is appropriate.
The failed 'minimal edit' check (ratio 0.741) is explained by the rule genuinely requiring a rewrite of the ownership sentence and deletion of the revocable licence — substance is minimal in effect.
Comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, cites the playbook position and offers the perpetual/irrevocable § 13.2-style licence fallback.
